resolveConflict_relation_rule.attack_too_strict: I could not construct a legitimate settler that is now refused. settlesDispute accepts three relations: the proposal declared the conflict in its own server-computed conflict_ids (the same relation applyChange already uses), or it edits any entity the conflict names as subject or blocked (ids are collected regardless of entity type or pinned revision), or it edits the same (entity,id,field) triple a conflicting draft edits. A genuine integration change that supersedes the disputed content still has the applyChange path, which prunes blocking_conflict_ids through conflict_ids. The one shape refused - a change that resolves the dispute semantically while touching nothing in the disputed scope and declaring nothing - is precisely the shape round 1 measured as a falsified record and demanded be refused.
resolveConflict_relation_rule.blocking_index_prune: the round-1/round-2 phantom-open-conflict defect is fixed at the source (resolveConflict now prunes and bumps ProjectState in the same transaction) and asserted twice (index read back, then a post-resolution freeze required to carry zero unresolved_items and not even contain the conflict id).

findings.N14_equivalence: ACCEPTED as an equivalent mutant. context.go:202 refuses 412 STALE_REVISION unless Hash(state.revision) == Hash(b.expected_project_state_revision); Hash is canonical-JSON sha, so any run that reaches the mutated assignment stores one of two Hash-equal (hence serialization-identical) values, and no assertion over the bundle can distinguish them. The distinguishing power lives in the guard itself, and the guard is mutation-covered (Z2 kills CTX-STALE-EXPECTED-REVISION-REJECTED, reproduced by both prior reviewers and present in the delivered round-3 matrix). I re-ran N14: PASS 282, survives exactly as disclosed. To refute the equivalence I would need an assertion comparing the stored revision to a value the CAS does not already force equal; none exists or could exist without weakening the CAS.
